objective: Simplify engine ownership, module and ABI boundaries, remove dead compatibility paths and inherited storage limits, preserve exact required behavior and measured performance.

accepted-freeze-plan.json.candidate: lazy body-motion cache with compact raw observations and unified wrapper construction

protocol.adoption: No REJECT in any workload guard; engine and default automatic upper 95% time-delta bounds below +0.5%. Report isolated stepping and WASM high-water memory. Require exact full parity and targeted ownership/ABI tests. Fixed counts; do not extend or restart an unchanged candidate to obtain acceptance.

accepted-freeze-plan.json.comparison: Frozen full source against baseline. Fresh identical-binary/source control and unchanged fixed cleanup criteria. All development failures retained. No speedup qualification is claimed.

body-motion-plan.json.hypothesis: The new cached-read check adds a native call to each of 284475 body-motion reads in default automatic. Returning the existing four-value motion observation from a single checked native operation can preserve the contract while removing repeated boundary transfers and JS loops. No frame-summary storage or solver arithmetic changes.
body-motion-plan.json.validation: Reject uncached reads, compare body motion exactly against the independent JS calculation across cached frames/branches; full structural gates if adopted.
body-motion-plan.json.diagnostic: Eight fixed full-source alternating fresh-process pairs, one warmup/one measured automatic cell61 compile per arm, against 2a5ef4f1. Not promotion. Then freeze a passing candidate for original 24/24/8 cleanup guards and fresh identical-binary control. Preserve all failed runs.

cache-read-plan.json.evidence: At identical native bytes, the revised wrapper costs about +0.80% in eight diagnostic pairs. The remaining regression is native. The new implementation examines optional trace state even on cache hits and on already-current-version reads.
cache-read-plan.json.invariant: Preparing a trace evicts its target immediately. A pending trace can become stale only when another version fills the shared cache; that necessarily changes the lineage current version. Therefore eviction is needed when reconciling versions, not on the same-version fast path. Fetch mutable trace state only when extending frames.
cache-read-plan.json.change: Remove the redundant Lineage.compute_to forwarding method, put the cache-extension check in frame_cache, and remove pending-trace inspection from update_computed when the current version already matches. Keep eviction after actual reconciliation and all ownership contracts.
cache-read-plan.json.validation: Interleaved version trace tests and ownership suite, then eight fixed paired full-source cell61 diagnostic rounds against baseline. No sample extension.

construction-plan.json.evidence: The native-call diagnostic still costs +1.33%. V8 object inspection shows Object.create-adopted wrappers use a different map/layout from constructed wrappers; Object.create also bypasses future class-field initializers. Trace requests are 195 frames versus 147209 charged frames in the default compile, so their state-copy routine is cold.
construction-plan.json.change: Use one constructor for both fresh and adopted handles, guarded by a private module token; native adoption remains unavailable to ordinary callers. Mark the existing trace-recording method cold and non-inlined to keep observation copies out of the common solver body. No duplicate solver specialization.
construction-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed full-source cell61 pairs against baseline after lifetime/trace tests. If passing, freeze this coherent implementation for full validation and the original fixed guards.

contact-observation-plan.json.trigger: The cache-hit simplification preserves interleaving but the eight-pair diagnostic still regresses +3.31%; no adoption.
contact-observation-plan.json.change: Make cached contact observation atomic in the native owner, like body motion. A presence read checks cache availability and event count once without copying any events. A full contact read checks and serializes in one native call. Remove the JS computedHandle layer and its duplicated native round-trip. Serialize full events through fixed three-value chunks to express the initialized output boundary without repeated variable indexing.
contact-observation-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed full-source cell61 pairs against baseline after cached-read/contact tests. Exact tracks and work; no sample extension.

contact-order-plan.json.trigger: Unified construction and cold trace recording reduce the diagnostic regression to +0.85%; still not adoptable.
contact-order-plan.json.design: There are exactly 65 ordered subsets of the four sled points. Represent that finite contact order with one byte per point in the native summary, and share precomputed immutable JS arrays by that value. This removes per-read point-list allocation and repeated copying. Contact line ids remain owned copies because their domain is unbounded. Mark sled-contact arrays readonly in the shared detector types; all existing consumers only read them.
contact-order-plan.json.scope: No per-frame JS cache or unbounded interning. The table is fixed by rider topology. Native frame summaries retain their previous size. Only pending traces are supplied to stepping; a completed observation is retained until a new request.
contact-order-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed full-source cell61 pairs after independent raw-frame/contact parity and lifetime tests. If promising, freeze for the original fixed guards and all structural checks; no sample extension.

diagnosis-plan.json.trigger: The fixed 24-pair full-source automatic guard rejected dev2: mean +3.7887%, 95% interval +3.573% to +4.013%, 24/24 slower. Do not adopt this candidate or repeat its unchanged runs.
diagnosis-plan.json.next: Finish the already-declared larger-budget and phase/memory runs. Profile earlier and changed source in the same disposable cwd, then use diagnostic ablations to identify extra boundary costs. Preserve the ownership contracts and exact tracks/work. Any revised candidate must be frozen and rechecked under the same fixed guard counts and limits.
diagnosis-plan.json.diagnosticComparisons: Eight fixed alternating warmed pairs per identified source ablation on automatic cell 61. Profiles and ablations are diagnosis, never promotion; do not extend them.

protocol.adoption: No REJECT in any workload guard; engine and default automatic upper 95% time-delta bounds below +0.5%. Report isolated stepping and WASM high-water memory. Require exact full parity and targeted ownership/ABI tests. Fixed counts; do not extend or restart an unchanged candidate to obtain acceptance.

freeze-plan.json.comparison: All candidate guards use --reference-root pointing to the clean baseline checkout. The fixed runner and input corpus are identical; both runtime source and binary changes are included. Control uses identical source and baseline binary. No speedup qualification is claimed.

motion-cache-plan.json.trigger: The finite contact-order table does not improve the diagnostic (+0.96%); reject it and retain straightforward owned point arrays.
motion-cache-plan.json.change: FrameCache owns all derived per-frame observations. Memoize the four-value body-motion result in a standard OnceCell in the frame summary, computing only on request. Shared snapshots may share this pure derived memo without copying simulation data; truncation/reset naturally discard it. Move the math out of the version arena into the cache. Avoid eager body-motion work in replay-only workloads.
motion-cache-plan.json.memory: Measure high-water linear memory and report the tradeoff of inline lazy observation storage; do not equate it with RSS.
motion-cache-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed full-source cell61 pairs, followed by an eight-pair engine diagnostic and memory diagnostic if promising. Exact observation/ownership tests before timing. Full original cleanup guards before adoption; no sample extension.

native-call-plan.json.trigger: Trace specialization leaves +1.58% and increases generated solver code. Reject the extra specialization and return to a single ordinary solver.
native-call-plan.json.change: Capture frequent native entry points as local function constants, avoiding repeated exports-object lookups through a live module binding. Use the exact signed-32-bit frame check matching the private ABI. Preserve disposed-handle and cached-read validation. Keep the already-correct compact raw summary.
native-call-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed full-source cell61 pairs against baseline after interface/lifetime tests. No sample extension.

output-buffers-plan.json.change: Replace inherited fixed candidate-window/event output arrays with reusable initialized vectors that grow only when needed. Keep fixed topology-sized state/trace buffers and bounded line-upload chunks. Remove the parallel single-line insertion ABI and require contact verification in workload checks.
output-buffers-plan.json.reason: The old window allocation inherited the retired batch simulator's layout, and fixed event capacity silently truncated cached output. Returned counts and frame spans should define logical output size.
output-buffers-plan.json.development: Eight paired macro and stepping diagnostics after three warmups, plus high-water memory. Then freeze under the original full-source cleanup guards; no speedup claim.

plan.json.purpose: Holistic engine simplification and stronger ownership boundaries; no new speedup claim.
changes: Separate frame-cache ownership from the version arena; name collision history for its actual role.
Give traces to their requesting version; keep the solver free of global observation state.
Remove the unused compiler batch simulator and its buffers, obsolete capability fallback, and redundant arena forwarding layer.
Introduce a typed private WASM adapter and explicit wrapper lifetimes; empty batches return their existing owner, disposed wrappers cannot alias reused handles.
Rename production cleanup and update all native callers without compatibility aliases; automate packaged-source discovery.
Measure wrapper changes with frozen source overlays through the existing paired-process scaffold. Keep the independent judge separate.

development.purpose: Diagnosis only, never promotion; archive unsuccessful variants.

finalGuards.adoption: No REJECT in any workload guard; engine and default automatic upper 95% time-delta bounds below +0.5%. Report isolated stepping and WASM high-water memory. Require exact full parity and targeted ownership/ABI tests. Fixed counts; do not extend or restart an unchanged candidate to obtain acceptance.

raw-summary-plan.json.evidence: The timed-interval profile shows repeated raw-frame reads and allocation remain substantial. The cache already deduplicates sled contact line ids for candidate windows, but each raw-frame read resends all collision triples and repeats this work in JS.
raw-summary-plan.json.change: Store the first-contact point order alongside the existing cached contact ids. Replace the mask field with a four-point array/count (fits existing FrameSummary padding), derive the window mask when needed, and return the compact summary directly for raw-frame reads. Borrow summaries instead of copying them. Keep all collision events for the public updates API and independent parity.
raw-summary-plan.json.validation: The expanded independent engine gate compares all raw frames, body motion and cached contact queries across 61115 saved frames. Native tests and wrapper lifetime/ABI tests must pass.
raw-summary-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed full-source cell61 pairs against the baseline after correctness checks. No sample extension; full original cleanup guards before adoption.

solver-boundary-plan.json.evidence: The previous binary keeps the non-history solver in its own approximately 12.9 KB function. After removing the unused batch simulator, LLVM folds that sole-use solver into the shared frame-cache reader, making that reader approximately 14.8 KB. Most calls to this reader only observe cached frames. Name-enabled profiles preserve non-code sections but not all instruction bytes; the function-size comparison is diagnostic.
solver-boundary-plan.json.hypothesis: Preserve the solver as a separate non-inlined routine. Keep frequently called cache reconciliation/lookup independent of the large stepping loop. This may recover the compiler cost without restoring dead code or weakening ownership checks.
solver-boundary-plan.json.diagnostic: One eight-pair full-source cell61 diagnostic against baseline after a locked build and correctness checks. Keep all failed variants; do not extend samples. If promising, freeze for the original full cleanup guards.

trace-specialization-plan.json.trigger: Compact raw summaries preserve exact independent observations and reduce the diagnostic regression to +1.71%, but do not yet satisfy adoption.
trace-specialization-plan.json.change: Specialize the solver for ordinary versus explicitly traced frames, selecting once per frame. Ordinary stepping does not need an observation pointer or history-shortcut resets; history reconstruction retains its existing tracking specialization. Keep one solver implementation and no runtime experiment switch.
trace-specialization-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed full-source cell61 pairs against baseline after trace, raw-frame and ownership tests. Report binary size and all failed variants. Full cleanup guards remain mandatory.

wrapper-access-plan.json.hypothesis: The single native body-motion read preserves correctness but still regresses automatic by 3.38%. Investigate JS hot-boundary access: use the handle itself as the single lifetime state (-1 when released) instead of a separate live flag, and capture the imported WASM instance in a local constant so frequent calls do not traverse a live module binding. Preserve all ownership checks.
wrapper-access-plan.json.diagnostic: Eight fixed paired full-source cell61 compiles against baseline, one warmup/one measured repetition. This is diagnosis, never promotion; preserve the failed body-motion result. No additional sample extension.

wrapper-isolation-plan.json.trigger: The explicit solver boundary still leaves a +2.84% default compile regression. Stop attributing the regression from profile shapes alone.
wrapper-isolation-plan.json.experiment: Run the current binary in both arms. Adapt only the earlier wrapper private ABI to current dynamic pointers and owned trace read; retain its previous ownership and read implementation. Compare it against the complete current wrapper/consumer source in the same directory. This diagnostic isolates the JS-side changes from native implementation cost. The adapted old wrapper is never eligible for adoption.
wrapper-isolation-plan.json.protocol: Eight fixed alternating fresh-process pairs, cell61, one warmup and one measured compile. Exact tracks/work required.

machine.acceptedBuild: locked cargo release, wasm32-unknown-unknown, plain Rust 1.95.0 in both arms; no wasm-opt or SIMD feature change
machine.isolation: Timings sequential on CPU 2 without concurrent builds, tests, parity or profiles. Normal desktop background processes remained.

developmentInterpretation.dev1: Separate cache ownership from version reconciliation; own traces per version; typed ABI adapter and explicit wrapper lifetimes; remove the unused batch simulator and forwarding layer. Macro/step diagnostics preserve fingerprints, reducing fixed memory by one page.
developmentInterpretation.dev2: Replace fixed window/event arrays with retained vectors, remove the redundant single-line ABI, automate manifest completeness, and freeze the complete source cleanup. The engine panel passes, but default automatic regresses 3.79% and the 750k workload regresses 1.17%. Reject this candidate. Its memory savings alone do not justify adoption.

diagnostics.name: body-motion
diagnostics.change: Return the four body-motion values through one checked native read, preserving arithmetic order.

diagnostics.name: wrapper-access
diagnostics.change: Consolidate handle liveness into a released sentinel; test a local instance alias, later removed.

diagnostics.name: solver-boundary
diagnostics.change: Outline the large solver to keep cached readers small.

diagnostics.name: wrapper-isolation
diagnostics.change: Hold the solver-boundary binary fixed in both arms; compare the earlier wrapper adapted only to the private ABI. This is not a baseline-binary comparison.

diagnostics.name: cache-read
diagnostics.change: Skip redundant trace eviction on same-version reads and remove the lineage forwarding method.

diagnostics.name: contact-observation
diagnostics.change: Check cached contact availability and read in one native operation; contact-presence queries avoid copying events.

diagnostics.name: raw-summary
diagnostics.change: Return already-deduplicated contact line IDs and first-contact point order from cached summaries.

diagnostics.name: trace-specialization
diagnostics.change: Try separate compile-time trace solver variants. Rejected; specialization removed.

diagnostics.name: native-call
diagnostics.change: Capture hot native functions locally and simplify signed frame validation; remove the extra trace specialization.

diagnostics.name: construction
diagnostics.change: Use one constructor with a private adoption token; outline cold trace recording. Adopted wrappers shrink from 56 to 32 bytes in the inspected V8 layout.

diagnostics.name: contact-order
diagnostics.change: Try interning the finite set of contact-point orders. No benefit over simpler owned arrays; removed.

diagnostics.name: motion-cache
diagnostics.change: Remove contact-order interning. Memoize pure body-motion observations lazily in FrameCache, shared safely with snapshots. This resolves the default-compile regression while preserving replay performance; report the inline storage cost.

developmentInterpretation.final: After the motion-cache diagnostic, format Rust and update module/observation documentation, rebuild and freeze the actual packaged artifact, then run full correctness gates and fresh fixed cleanup guards. Do not extend or restart any unchanged run.

profiles.interpretation: Profiles are diagnostic, not timing decisions. Name-enabled builds differ in code layout, so function mapping distinguishes exact function-body matches from approximate index labels. Timed-region profiles exclude module load/warmup but include compileWorker setup beyond compileMs. Raw profiles remain in the local study directory. V8 layout inspection measures wrapper instance shape, not total heap usage.
